results.title: Weakly inaccessible cardinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A cardinal κ is *weakly inaccessible* if it is an uncountable, regular limit cardinal.

results.title: Set of inaccessible cardinals below a cardinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: InAccBelow κ is the set of all inaccessible cardinals below κ.

results.title: Inaccessible fixed point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A cardinal κ is an *inaccessible fixed point* if κ is inaccessible and the inaccessibles below κ have order type κ (i.e. κ is the κ-th inaccessible).

results.title: The beth hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Below an inaccessible `κ`, the beth hierarchy stays below `κ`: `κ` is a beth fixed point (`IsInaccessible.beth_ord`) and `beth` is strictly monotone.

results.title: The aleph hierarchy stays below an inaccessible cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Below an inaccessible `κ`, the aleph hierarchy stays below `κ`: same argument via `IsInaccessible.aleph_ord`.

results.title: At most $\kappa$ inaccessible cardinals lie below $\kappa$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are at most `κ` inaccessibles below `κ`: the set injects into `↥(Set.Iio κ.ord)`, which has size `lift κ`. The `≤` half of the counting needed for the Mahlo-implies-fixed-point benchmark item.

results.title: Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Regular cardinals are unbounded below an uncountable limit cardinal `κ` (in particular a weakly inaccessible one): above any `a < κ` sits `succ (max a ℵ₀)`, regular by `isRegular_succ` and below `κ` since `κ` is a limit.

results.title: Under GCH, weakly inaccessible cardinals are inaccessible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under (local) GCH, weakly inaccessible implies strongly inaccessible: for infinite `μ < κ`, `2 ^ μ = succ μ < κ` by the limit property, and the finite case is `power_lt_aleph0`.

results.title: Strong limit cardinals are closed under exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A strong limit `κ` is closed under cardinal exponentiation: `x ^ y ≤ 2 ^ (x * y)` (via `cantor` and `power_mul`), and `x * y < κ` by `mul_lt_of_lt`. No infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by `IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.

results.title: Existence of an inaccessible with no inaccessibles below it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If any inaccessible exists, some inaccessible has no inaccessibles below it: minimize over the initial ordinals of inaccessible cardinals (`WellFounded.has_min`), and any member of `inaccessibleBelow` would give a smaller one.

results.title: Weak power below a strong limit cardinal equals the cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `2 ≤ x < κ` with `κ` a strong limit, `x ^< κ = κ`: every smaller power is below `κ` (`IsStrongLimit.power_lt`), while every `y < κ` sits below `2 ^ y ≤ x ^< κ`. No infiniteness hypothesis is needed — it is automatic by `IsStrongLimit.aleph0_le`.

results.title: Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Strong limits are unbounded below an inaccessible `κ`: above any `a < κ` sits `ℶ_{a.ord + ω}`, a strong limit by `isStrongLimit_beth` since `a.ord + ω` is a limit ordinal (`isSuccLimit_add`), and below `κ` since `(a.ord + ω).card = a.ord.card + ℵ₀ < κ` (`add_lt_of_lt`).

results.title: Set of regular cardinals below a cardinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The regular cardinals below `κ`, carried as initial ordinals — parallel to `inaccessibleBelow`, and definitionally the stationary set in `IsWeaklyMahlo`. Spelled with Mathlib's `Ordinal.IsInitial`.

results.title: A regular beth fixed point is uncountable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A regular beth fixed point is uncountable: regularity gives `ℵ₀ ≤ κ`, and `κ = ℵ₀` fails the fixed-point equation since `ℶ_ω > ℶ_0 = ℵ₀`.

results.title: A regular beth fixed point is inaccessible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Converse to `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`: a regular beth fixed point is inaccessible. Uncountability is derived, not assumed (`aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`); for `x < κ`, `2 ^ x ≤ 2 ^ ℶ_{x.ord} = ℶ_{succ x.ord} < κ`, using that `κ.ord` is a limit ordinal.

results.title: Inaccessible cardinals are the regular beth fixed points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `κ` is inaccessible iff it is regular and a beth fixed point (uncountability is automatic by `aleph0_lt_of_isRegular_beth_ord`): this packages `of_isRegular_beth_ord` with Mathlib's `IsInaccessible.beth_ord`.

results.title: Exactly $\kappa$ inaccessibles lie below an inaccessible fixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fixed-point equation forces `#(inaccessibleBelow κ) = lift κ` (`card_type`): the companion to the upper bound `mk_inaccessibleBelow_le`.

results.title: Inaccessibles are unbounded below an inaccessible fixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Inaccessibles below an inaccessible fixed point are unbounded: if they were bounded by `a`, the set would inject into `Iic a.val`, hence have size at most `lift (a.val + 1).card < lift κ` — contradicting `mk_inaccessibleBelow`.

results.title: Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible cardinal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Limit cardinals are unbounded below a weakly inaccessible `κ`: the sup of the `ω`-chain `μ 0 = succ (max a ℵ₀)`, `μ (n+1) = succ (μ n)` stays below `κ` (`sum_lt_of_isRegular`), exceeds `a`, and is a limit since every `x < σ` lies below some `μ n` (`exists_lt_of_lt_ciSup`).

results.title: Supremum of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sup of a bounded set of initial ordinals is initial: if `σ.card.ord < σ` then some member exceeds `σ.card.ord`, trapping it strictly between itself and its own initial ordinal.

results.title: Reciprocal polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_d x^d$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is *reciprocal* (palindromic) if it equals its reversal $x^d f(1/x)$, that is, if $a_i = a_{d-i}$ for all $0 \le i \le d$.

results.title: Characterization of reciprocal polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is reciprocal if and only if its reversal $x^d f(1/x)$ equals $f$.

results.title: 0,1-polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a *$0,1$-polynomial* if every coefficient of $f$ is $0$ or $1$.

results.title: Characterization of 0,1-polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a $0,1$-polynomial if and only if, for every $n \ge 0$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in $f$ is $0$ or $1$.

results.title: Non-cyclotomic polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is *non-cyclotomic* if $f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$ denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial.

results.title: Characterization of non-cyclotomic polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is non-cyclotomic if and only if $f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$ denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial.

results.title: Irreducibility under repeated squaring of the variable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic $0,1$-polynomial with fewer than $15$ nonzero coefficients. Then $f(x^{2^n})$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Capelli's theorem for $f(x^r)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and let $r \ge 2$ be an integer. Then $f(x^r)$ is reducible if and only if either $f(x^p)$ is reducible for some prime $p$ dividing $r$, or $4$ divides $r$ and $f(x^4)$ is reducible. Here reducible means not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Square compositions of $0,1$-polynomials modulo $4$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. If $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, then $f(x^2) \equiv f(x)\,f(-x) \pmod 4$ as polynomials, that is, the two polynomials have the same image in $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})[x]$.

results.title: Reducibility of $f(x^4)$ and $f(x^2)$ for $0,1$-polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and of positive degree, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. Then $f(x^4)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ if and only if $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: Newton sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $a, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$. The sequence $a$ is a Newton sequence generated by $c$ if for every natural number $n$, $a_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_{n-j} c_{j+1} + (n+1) c_{n+1}$.

results.title: The recurrence of a Newton sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $a, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be such that $a$ is a Newton sequence generated by $c$. Then for every natural number $n$ we have $a_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} a_{n-j} c_{j+1} + (n+1) c_{n+1}$.

results.title: Power-growth exceptional set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and real numbers $p$ and $x_0$, this is the set of real numbers $x \ge x_0$ such that $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, where $h(x)^p$ is the real power and $h'(x)$ is the derivative of $h$ at $x$, taken to be $0$ where $h$ is not differentiable.

results.title: The power-growth exceptional set has finite measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p > 1$ and $x_0$ be real numbers, and let $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously differentiable, with $h(x) > 0$ for all $x \ge x_0$ and $h$ nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$. Then the power-growth exceptional set of $h$, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, has finite Lebesgue measure.

results.title: Wiman Taylor coefficient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin is $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$, where $f^{(n)}$ is the $n$th iterated complex derivative of $f$.

results.title: Wiman term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a real number $r$ and a natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$ is the real number $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin. It is the modulus of the $n$th Taylor term of $f$ on the circle of radius $|r|$.

results.title: Wiman maximum term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term $\mu(f, r)$ is the supremum over $n \in \mathbb{N}$ of the Wiman terms $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Wiman Taylor coefficient of $f$.

results.title: Wiman maximum modulus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus $M(f, r)$ is the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = |r|$.

results.title: Wiman term at the absolute value of the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.

results.title: Wiman maximum term at the absolute value of the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.

results.title: Wiman maximum modulus at the absolute value of the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

results.title: Wiman term at a negated radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $-r$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.

results.title: The Wiman maximum term is even in the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.

results.title: The Wiman maximum modulus is even in the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

results.title: Transcendental functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is transcendental when there is no complex polynomial $p$ with $f(z) = p(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Values on a circle are bounded by the maximum modulus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous, let $r$ be a real number and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = r$. Then $|f(z)| \le M(f, r)$, where $M(f, r)$ is the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

results.title: Cubing a Wiman 2/3 bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $\mu$ be real numbers with $M \ge 0$, $\mu \ge 0$ and $\log \mu \ge 0$, where $\log$ is the real logarithm with $\log 0 = 0$. If $M \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$, then $M^3 \le \mu^3 (\log \mu)^2$.

results.title: Absorbing constants into the exponent gap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $C > 0$ there is a real $U > 1$ such that for all reals $\mu$ and $A$ with $U \le \mu \le A$ and $A \le C \mu \bigl(1 + (\log A)^{81/128}\bigr)$, we have $A \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$.

results.title: The maximum modulus is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $r \ge 0$. Then there is a point $z$ with $|z| = r$ such that $|f(w)| \le |f(z)|$ for every $w$ with $|w| = r$, and the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|w| = r} |f(w)|$ equals $|f(z)|$.

results.title: Radial majorant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and a real number $r$, the radial majorant of $f$ at $r$ is $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$, the sum of the radial Taylor terms at radius $|r|$. By convention $M_f(r) = 0$ when this series diverges.

results.title: Radial Taylor terms are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $0 \le |a_n| \, |r|^n$.

results.title: Summability of the radial Taylor terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every real $r$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ converges.

results.title: The radial majorant is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and every real number $r$, the radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ (taken to be $0$ when the series diverges) satisfies $0 \le M_f(r)$.

results.title: Each radial Taylor term is at most the radial majorant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{k \ge 0} |a_k| \, |r|^k$ be its radial majorant. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n| \, |r|^n \le M_f(r)$.

results.title: Wiman growth function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ be its radial majorant, taken to be $0$ when the series diverges. For a real number $x$, the Wiman growth of $f$ at $x$ is $\log M_f(e^x)$, the logarithm of the radial majorant at radius $e^x$, with the convention $\log 0 = 0$.

results.title: Wiman coefficient measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, the Wiman coefficient measure of $f$ is the measure $\mu_f = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n|\,\delta_n$ on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n$ mass $|a_n|$.

results.title: Tilted coefficient measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, with mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For a real number $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ is the exponential tilt of $\mu_f$ by $n \mapsto xn$: the measure with density $e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$.

results.title: Point masses of the Wiman coefficient measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $\mu_f(\{n\}) = |a_n|$.

results.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure are finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ mass $|a_n|$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every real $x$, the function $n \mapsto e^{xn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.

results.title: The exponential-integrability set of the Wiman coefficient measure is the whole line
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. The set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$ is all of $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Every real parameter is interior to the exponential-integrability set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. Every real $x$ lies in the interior of the set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.

results.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure equal the Wiman majorant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$,

results.title: Moment generating function of the coefficient measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which has mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For every real $x$, the moment generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the radial majorant $M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$.

results.title: The Wiman growth is the cumulant generating function of the coefficient measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the cumulant generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\log \int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the Wiman growth $G_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f$ is the Wiman majorant of $f$.

results.title: A nonzero Taylor coefficient makes the Wiman coefficient measure nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. If $a_n \ne 0$ for some $n$, then the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ is not the zero measure.

results.title: The Wiman tilted measure is a probability measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function such that $f^{(n)}(0)/n! \ne 0$ for some $n$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the Wiman tilted measure of $f$ at $x$, which has density $n \mapsto e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$, is a probability measure.

results.title: Atoms of the tilted coefficient measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).

results.title: Atomic form of the tilted coefficient measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ equals $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \frac{T_n(e^x)}{M_f(e^x)}\,\delta_n$, the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ at each $n$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).

results.title: The logarithmic majorant is $C^2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$ be the logarithm of its radial Taylor majorant at radius $e^x$ (with $\log 0 = 0$). Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi'(x) = \int n \, d
u_x(n)$, the mean of $n$ under $
u_x$.

results.title: Second derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi''(x)$ is the variance of $n$ under $
u_x$.

results.title: The logarithmic majorant has nonnegative second derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi''(x) \ge 0$ for every real $x$.

results.title: The Taylor terms are bounded above
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $r$ be real. Then the set of Taylor terms $\{|a_n|\,|r|^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is bounded above.

results.title: Each Taylor term is at most the maximum term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_k |a_k|\,|r|^k$. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le \mu(r)$.

results.title: Bounding the maximum term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For all real $r$ and $c$, $\mu(r) \le c$ if and only if $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le c$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: The maximum term is attained by a Taylor term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $r$ there is an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|a_n|\,|r|^n = \mu(r)$.

results.title: Corrected Rosenbloom estimate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For every real $x$, $M_f(e^x) \le 8\,\mu_f(e^x)\,\bigl(1 + \sqrt{g_f''(x)}\bigr)$.

results.title: Cauchy's inequality for the maximum term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$. Then $\mu(r) \le M(r)$ for every real $r > 0$.

results.title: Taylor expansion of an entire function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ converges unconditionally to $f(z)$.

results.title: Transcendental entire functions have infinitely many Taylor coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A transcendental entire function has infinitely many nonzero Taylor coefficients.

results.title: The maximum modulus is at most the radial Taylor majorant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and let $r \ge 0$. Then the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = r} |f(z)|$ satisfies $M(r) \le \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| r^n$.

results.title: The maximum term of a transcendental entire function tends to infinity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then $\mu(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$.

results.title: The maximum term eventually exceeds one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\mu(r) > 1$ for all real $r \ge R$.

results.title: The logarithm of the maximum term is eventually positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\log \mu(r) > 0$ for all real $r \ge R$.

results.title: Eventual regularity of the logarithmic majorant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$, $\Phi'(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$, and there is a real $x_0$ such that $\Phi(x) > 0$ for every $x \ge x_0$ and both $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ are nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$.

results.title: Wiman exceptional set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with radial majorant $M_f$, let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$, the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$ is the union of the power-growth bad sets of $g$ and of $g'$ with exponent $9/8$ above $x_0$, that is, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or $g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$.

results.title: The Wiman exceptional set has finite measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function, let $M_f$ be its radial majorant and let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ let $E_f(x_0)$ be the Wiman exceptional set, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or $g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$. There is $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue measure and $g''(x) \le g(x)^{81/64}$ for every $x \ge x_0$ outside $E_f(x_0)$.

results.title: Majorant bound off an exceptional set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. There are reals $C > 0$ and $x_0$ such that the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue measure and, for every real $x \ge x_0$ with $x \notin E_f(x_0)$,…

results.title: The maximum term tends to infinity along logarithmic radii
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then $\mu(e^x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: Wiman's inequality with exponent $2/3$ at arbitrarily large radii
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$ and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then for every real $R$ there is a real $r > R$ with $M(r) \le \mu(r) (\log \mu(r))^{2/3}$.

results.title: Atoms are the jumps of the cdf
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$, and for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ let $F(x^-) = \lim_{y \to x^-} F(y)$ be its left limit at $x$. Then $\mu(\{x\})$ equals the jump $F(x) - F(x^-)$, which is a nonnegative real number since $F$ is nondecreasing.

results.title: The cdf is continuous exactly at the non-atoms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. For every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $F$ is continuous at $x$ if and only if $\mu(\{x\}) = 0$.

results.title: No atom at a continuity point of the cdf
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. If $F$ is continuous at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}$, then $\mu(\{x\}) = 0$.

results.title: Continuity points of the cdf have null boundary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. If $F$ is continuous at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}$, then the boundary of the half-line $(-\infty, x]$, which is $\{x\}$, has $\mu$-measure zero.

results.title: Mass of a half-open interval via the cdf
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, the measure $\mu((a, b])$ equals $\max(F(b) - F(a), 0)$, as an extended nonnegative real.

results.title: The continuity points of the cdf are dense
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F(y) = \mu((-\infty, y])$. The set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}$ at which $F$ is continuous is dense in $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Tournament
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A tournament on the players $1, \dots, n$ is a binary relation $T$, where $T(i, j)$ means that $i$ beats $j$, such that no player beats itself and for any two distinct players $i$ and $j$ exactly one of $T(i, j)$ and $T(j, i)$ holds.

results.title: Score of a player
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a binary relation on the players $1, \dots, n$, where $T(i, j)$ means that $i$ beats $j$. The score of a player $i$ is the number of players $j$ such that $T(i, j)$ holds, that is, the number of players that $i$ beats.

results.title: Reducible tournament
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A tournament is reducible if some nonempty proper set of players loses all games against the complement.

results.title: Circular triad
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a binary relation on the players $1, \dots, n$, where $T(i, j)$ means that $i$ beats $j$. A set $S$ of players is a circular triad of $T$ if $S$ has exactly three elements and every $i \in S$ beats exactly one $j \in S$.

results.title: Exponential generating function of a shifted binomial sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, let $g(n) = n! \binom{n-a+b}{b}$ for $n \ge a$ and $g(n) = 0$ for $n < a$, and let $A(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} g(n) x^n / n!$ be its exponential generating function, a formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $(1 - x)^{b+1} A(x) = x^a$; equivalently, $A(x) = x^a (1 - x)^{-(b+1)}$.

results.title: Landau's theorem on score sequences
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s_1 \le s_2 \le \dots \le s_n$ be a nondecreasing sequence of natural numbers. There is a tournament on $n$ players in which player $i$ has score $s_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i \ge \binom{k}{2}$ for every $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i = \binom{n}{2}$.

results.title: Moon's reducibility criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a tournament on $n$ players in which the score $s_i$ of player $i$ satisfies $s_1 \le s_2 \le \dots \le s_n$. Then $T$ is reducible if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i = \binom{k}{2}$ for some integer $k$ with $1 \le k < n$.

results.title: Moon's count of circular triads
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a tournament on $n$ players with scores $s_1, \dots, s_n$, the number of circular triads is $\binom{n}{3} - \sum_{i=1}^{n} \binom{s_i}{2}$.

results.title: Cost of an edit script

results.title: Edit-distance result record
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An edit-distance result over a type $\alpha$ consists of a natural number, the reported distance, and an edit script over $\alpha$.

results.title: Edit-distance cost counters
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An edit-distance cost record is a pair of natural numbers: the number of dynamic-programming table cells initialized or transitioned, and the number of operations emitted while reconstructing an edit script.

results.title: Total edit-distance cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total of an edit-distance cost record is the number of table cells initialized or transitioned plus the number of operations emitted during reconstruction.

results.title: Edit distance algorithm
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given lists $s = s_1 \cdots s_m$ and $t = t_1 \cdots t_n$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the algorithm fills a table $D(i, j)$ for $0 \le i \le m$ and $0 \le j \le n$ by $D(0, j) = j$, $D(i, 0) = i$ and $D(i, j) = \min(D(i-1, j-1) + c_{ij}, D(i-1, j) + 1, D(i, j-1) + 1)$ for $i, j \ge 1$, where $c_{ij}$ is $0$ if the test reports $s_i = t_j$ and $1$ otherwise. results.title: Correctness of the returned edit script
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the edit script returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ transforms $s$ into $t$.

results.title: The returned edit script realizes the distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the unit cost of the edit script returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ equals the distance it returns.

results.title: Minimality of the computed edit distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality. Every edit script that transforms $s$ into $t$ has unit cost at least the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$.

results.title: Edit distance from the empty list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from the empty list to $t$ is the length of $t$.

results.title: Edit distance to the empty list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $s$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from $s$ to the empty list is the length of $s$.

results.title: Edit distance of a list to itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $s$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from $s$ to $s$ is $0$.

results.title: Edit distance vanishes only on equal lists
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the distance returned by the dynamic-programming edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is $0$ if and only if $s = t$.

results.title: Table cost of the edit distance algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, write $|s|$ and $|t|$ for their lengths. The number of table-cell transitions charged by the dynamic-programming edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is exactly $(|s| + 1)(|t| + 1)$, one per pair of a prefix of $s$ and a prefix of $t$.

results.title: Reconstruction cost of the edit distance algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the number of reconstruction steps charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ equals the length of the edit script it returns.

results.title: Reconstruction cost bound for edit distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, write $|s|$ and $|t|$ for their lengths. The number of reconstruction steps charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is at most $|s| + |t|$.

results.title: Running time of the edit distance algorithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the total number of events charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$, that is its cell transitions plus its reconstruction steps, equals $(|s| + 1)(|t| + 1) + k$, where $k$ is the length of the edit script it returns.

results.title: Every edit script has an inverse of the same cost
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every script has an inverse of the same cost (swap insertions and deletions, reverse substitutions).

results.title: Composition of edit scripts is subadditive in cost
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two scripts compose into one whose cost is at most the sum of their costs.

results.title: Symmetry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Symmetry of unit-cost edit distance.

results.title: The triangle inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The triangle inequality for unit-cost edit distance.

results.title: Edit distance between distinct lists is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Distinct lists are at positive distance.

results.title: f2 statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statistic `f2 X Y = 𝔼[(p X - p Y) ^ 2]`, the expected squared allele-frequency difference between populations `X` and `Y`.

results.title: f3 statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statistic `f3 C A B = 𝔼[(p C - p A) * (p C - p B)]` of a target population `C` against two source populations `A` and `B`.

results.title: f4 statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statistic `f4 A B C D = 𝔼[(p A - p B) * (p C - p D)]`.

results.title: f2 of a population with itself is zero
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Symmetry of the f2 statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2` is symmetric.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the f2 statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2` is nonnegative.

results.title: f4 is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4` is symmetric under exchanging the two pairs.

results.title: f4 changes sign when the first pair is swapped
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4` changes sign when the first pair is swapped.

results.title: f4 changes sign when the second pair is swapped
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4` changes sign when the second pair is swapped.

results.title: f2 as a special case of f4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2` is the special case `f4 A B A B`.

results.title: f3 as a special case of f4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f3` is the special case `f4 C A C B`.

results.title: Square of a difference of square-integrable frequencies is integrable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A difference of square-integrable frequencies has integrable square.

results.title: f3 in terms of f2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f3` in terms of `f2`: `f3 C A B = (f2 C A + f2 C B - f2 A B) / 2`.

results.title: f4 in terms of f2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4` in terms of `f2`: `f4 A B C D = (f2 A D + f2 B C - f2 A C - f2 B D) / 2`.

results.title: Admixture-graph drift model
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: The admixture-graph drift model, stated at the level of second moments.

results.title: Allele frequency of a population in the drift model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The allele frequency of population `X`: the root frequency plus the weighted sum of the drift increments of the edges traversed by lineages from `X`.

results.title: Drift lengths are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Drift lengths are nonnegative.

results.title: Weighted sum of drift increments is square integrable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A weighted sum of increments is square integrable.

results.title: Population frequencies are square integrable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Population frequencies are square integrable.

results.title: Bilinearity of the second moment of drift increments
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Bilinearity of the second moment of increments: `𝔼[(∑ e, a e * incr e) * (∑ f, b f * incr f)] = ∑ e, a e * b e * len e`.

results.title: f4 in the drift model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4` in the drift model: the root cancels, and `f4 A B C D` is the drift length shared by the paths `A–B` and `C–D`, weighted by `(w A e - w B e) * (w C e - w D e)`.

results.title: f2 in the drift model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2` in the drift model: `f2 X Y = ∑ e, (w X e - w Y e) ^ 2 * len e`.

results.title: f3 in the drift model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f3` in the drift model: `f3 C A B = ∑ e, (w C e - w A e) * (w C e - w B e) * len e`.

results.title: f4 vanishes for edge-disjoint paths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f4 A B C D = 0` when no edge contributes to both the `A–B` and the `C–D` path. On a tree with split `AB | CD` the paths `A–B` and `C–D` share no edge, so this hypothesis holds.

results.title: Binary loadings of a drift model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The model has binary loadings if every lineage weight is `0` or `1`.

results.title: Lineage of a population in the drift model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The edges of weight `1` for population `X`; on a tree, the root-to-`X` lineage.

results.title: f3 is nonnegative under binary loadings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With binary loadings `f3` is nonnegative; on a tree it is the drift length of the path from `C` to the `A–B` path.

results.title: f2 as a symmetric-difference drift length under binary loadings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With binary loadings `f2 X Y` is the total drift length of the edges in exactly one of the weight-`1` edge sets of `X` and `Y`. On a tree, where these sets are the root-to-`X` and root-to-`Y` paths, this is the additive tree distance between `X` and `Y`.

results.title: Three-population test: negative f3 rules out a tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Three-population test: a negative `f3 C A B` is incompatible with binary loadings, hence with every tree model.

results.title: f3 of a pure admixture
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `C` is a mixture of `A` and `B` in proportions `α : 1 - α` (with no subsequent drift), then `f3 C A B = -α (1 - α) f2 A B`.

results.title: f3 of an admixture followed by drift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Admixture followed by drift: if `C` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` that then drifts along a private edge `c` (not traversed by `A` or `B`), then `f3 C A B = len c - α (1 - α) f2 A B`; post-admixture drift can mask the admixture signal.

results.title: Nondegenerate pure admixture gives negative f3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Three-population test, converse direction: a nondegenerate pure admixture (`0 < α < 1`, `f2 A B > 0`) yields a negative `f3 C A B`.

results.title: f4 of an admixed population scales with the mixture proportion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `X` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `Y` and `C`, then `f4 A O X C = α * f4 A O Y C` (bilinearity of `f4`, together with `f4 A O C C = 0`).

results.title: f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: f4-ratio estimation of the admixture proportion. f4-ratio estimation (Patterson et al. 2012). Let `X` be an `α : 1 - α` mixture of a source lineage `Y` and of `C`, where `Y` is unsampled but sister to the sampled population `B` relative to the `A–O` path, so that `f4 A O Y C = f4 A O B C`. If this value is nonzero, the ratio `f4 A O X C / f4 A O B C` of two estimable statistics recovers the admixture proportion `α`.

results.title: Mean allele frequency of a subdivided population
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Mean allele frequency `q̄ = ∑ i, c i * q i` of a population made of subpopulations with weights `c i` and allele frequencies `q i`.

results.title: Mean within-subpopulation heterozygosity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Mean within-subpopulation (Hardy–Weinberg) heterozygosity `H_S = ∑ i, c i * 2 q i (1 - q i)`.

results.title: Total heterozygosity of the pooled population
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Total heterozygosity `H_T = 2 q̄ (1 - q̄)` expected under random mating of the pooled population.

results.title: Wahlund identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Wahlund identity: for weights summing to `1`, `H_T - H_S = 2 ∑ i, c i * (q i - q̄) ^ 2`, twice the weighted variance of subpopulation frequencies.

results.title: Wahlund effect
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Wahlund effect: with nonnegative weights summing to `1`, subdivision lowers heterozygosity, `H_S ≤ H_T`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the fixation index $F_{ST}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `F_ST = (H_T - H_S) / H_T` is nonnegative for nonnegative weights summing to `1`. The ratio is defined only when `H_T > 0` (at a fixed allele `H_T = H_S = 0`), so that is assumed.
